External save conflicts never overwrite silently
Dirty content survives window restart
Text, image and Markdown preview have safe fallbacks

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-23: 33 frontend test files, 650 cases, 2283 frontend modules, 2118 bundle sources, 203 recorded migration-debt files and Rust 293/293.
All Browser E2E scenarios passed 22/22 (19 carried over from S1-S5 plus 3 new S7 scenarios: editor-group split, PNG binary-fallback placeholder, Markdown plain-text fallback).

Each S1-S5 slice additionally passed a focused repeat (--repeat-each=3, --retries=0) of its own new scenario(s) before the full-suite run; S7's three new scenarios likewise passed --repeat-each=3 --retries=0 (9/9) before the full-suite run.
nativeScenarios: F030 registered no new real-desktop scenarios of its own in this slice; the real Tauri/WKWebView edit-and-save chain (open via the system folder picker, create/edit/save an exact-byte file, verify on disk) was already established during the F020 single-root desktop acceptance and is the native evidence this feature continues to rely on.

F030's own desktop matrix (kill-9 restart recovery, real CloseRequested close handshake, on-disk backup directory audit) is registered as E2E-003 in docs/e2e-handover.md and handed over to Codex for native execution; it has not yet been executed.
platformGaps: E2E-003 in docs/e2e-handover.md (real hot-exit restart recovery, external-conflict Cmd+S save, and orphan-decoration desktop matrix) is handed over to Codex and not yet executed.

The real Rust WindowEvent::CloseRequested close handshake (veto until the last throttled backup is confirmed flushed, then allow close) is not implemented; PlainWorkingCopyBackupTracker.onFinalBeforeShutdown always returns false, so a normal window close may lose the most recent throttled backup write. This is declared as a known-current-state, not-a-regression condition in E2E-003 and tracked as a follow-up item in docs/e2e-handover.md.

S2's externally-deleted-open-file DELETED detection uses a bounded per-root LRU (256 entries) of resources seen through plainReadFile as an approximation of "currently open files", not a precise open-editor/working-copy reference count; root revocation does not proactively clear this LRU, it only shrinks lazily as new reads evict old entries (harmless because the revoked root stops receiving wakes), so the approximation can lazily retain entries past root removal.

The two new S5 frontend files (plain-workspace-backup-service.ts, plain-workspace-backup-tracker.ts) reuse and minimally extend existing Harness closed-set checks (MIDDLE_SERVICE_DESCRIPTORS, ALLOWED_MONACO_APP_IMPORTS, isAllowedBridgeIdentifier) rather than adding a dedicated AST hostile-mutation suite of the density used by earlier F020 slices; only the real source passing the existing checks was used as positive evidence.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Open, preview, pin, split, edit and save files
acceptanceResults.result: Open/edit/save are covered by the existing F020 versioned read/write chain and the S3/S5 Browser E2E for dirty tracking and save; preview and pin are covered by the S1 Browser E2E (single-click preview replaces the previous preview tab, double-click or edited content promotes it to pinned). Splitting an editor into multiple groups is now covered by the S7 Browser E2E ('splits an editor into two groups that stay in sync while editing...'): the real Ctrl/Cmd+\ `workbench.action.splitEditor` keybinding produces a second `.editor-group-container` (the real `active`/`inactive` DOM markers `EditorGroupView#setActive` toggles), both groups show a tab for the same resource, editing either side's own Monaco widget updates the other instantly and dirties both tabs together (same shared working copy), a single Ctrl/Cmd+S clears both, and closing the split side's sole tab auto-removes the now-empty group (default closeEmptyGroups) back to one group with the saved content intact. This is still unmodified, inherited default Workbench behavior that F030 did not patch or instrument, but it is no longer an unverified gap.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: External save conflicts never overwrite silently

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Dirty content survives window restart

This is a simulated reload of the mock persistence layer, not a real OS process kill/relaunch against the Rust backup store; the real kill-9-and-relaunch desktop variant is registered as E2E-003 and not yet executed.

features.name: Quick Open, workspace search and replace
acceptance: File and content search honor ignore and include/exclude rules
Results stream and cancel without blocking the UI
Replace plan validates file versions before writes

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-23: 38 frontend test files, 725 cases, 2300 frontend modules, 2134 bundle sources, 203 recorded migration-debt files and Rust 345/345.

All Browser E2E scenarios passed 32/32 (31 carried over from S1-S4 plus 1 new F040 S5 scenario proving the search.exclude default excludes a node_modules directory from both Quick Open file search and Search view text search).
The new S5 scenario additionally passed a focused repeat (--repeat-each=3, --retries=0) before the full-suite run, matching every earlier slice's own acceptance discipline.
nativeScenarios: F040 introduces no changes to the native file open/read/save IPC surface: Quick Open's "open match" and every replace path's per-resource save both route through the exact same native workspace read and versioned-write (wv1/PLR1/PLW1) chain already validated at native desktop level during F020/F030's own acceptance (system folder picker, exact-byte CRUD, versioned save conflict handling). No native-desktop scenario was executed specifically for F040's own additions in this feature -- the bounded Rust file/text-search traversal, gitignore/exclude matching, streaming wake/poll/cancel protocol, and replace coordinator are all new Rust/TypeScript surface with no prior native evidence to inherit.

F040's own desktop matrix -- real large-directory search performance and cancellation responsiveness, real multi-layer .gitignore/search.exclude effectiveness at real disk scale, Cmd+P open-from-large-tree, and a real version-conflict replace path with on-disk verification -- is registered as E2E-004 in docs/e2e-handover.md and handed over to Codex for native execution; it has not yet been executed.
platformGaps: E2E-004 in docs/e2e-handover.md (real large-directory search performance/cancellation, real multi-layer .gitignore/search.exclude effectiveness, Cmd+P open-from-large-tree, and a real version-conflict replace path with on-disk verification) is handed over to Codex and not yet executed.

Rust's regex engine (the `regex` crate) is linear-time only: no PCRE2, lookaround, or backreference support in search patterns, narrower than upstream's optional PCRE2 mode; an invalid or unsupported pattern surfaces as a Warning message rather than being silently accepted or crashing.

Replace substitutes text literally and does not support `$1`-style capture-group backreferences in the replacement text -- Rust does not return capture groups to the frontend (a deliberate narrowing, stated alongside the regex limitation above, not hidden).

Replacing across multiple files produces one independent undo entry per file rather than one shared cross-file undo group -- a deliberate isolation trade-off (F040 S4) so one file's save failure never blocks or rolls back another file's successful replace.

`search.useIgnoreFiles`/`search.useGlobalIgnoreFiles`/`search.useParentIgnoreFiles` have no registered configuration schema; Rust's search domain hardcodes "always honor .gitignore, never global/parent ignore files" and reads no such flag from any request DTO, so registering a schema for settings neither side consumes was judged actively misleading rather than treated as a completeness gap (F040 S5 decision).

Symlink exclusion from search results is proven by 3 Rust unit tests (F040 S2) and one browser-mock-level unit test (tests/unit/workspace-search-bridge.test.ts, "never reports a symlink as a match and never traverses through one"), not by a live Browser/Playwright scenario -- the shared installNativeIpcMock fixture helper used by every Browser E2E test does not expose symlink-node injection through its extraFiles parameter, and adding that plumbing was judged to risk the ~30 other scenarios sharing it for marginal signal beyond the existing unit-level proof against the identical mock code.

"Replace All in File" (per-file granularity) shares its code path with "Replace" and "Replace All", both of which have dedicated Browser E2E coverage, but it has no dedicated Browser E2E scenario of its own (F040 S4 decision; unit tests and code review cover its shared logic).
An over-8-MiB unopened file's replace failure has no dedicated Browser E2E of its own; the underlying 8 MiB read limit itself is already covered by earlier workspace read slices (F020).

Root-relative search results are not paired with a rootId in the wire response (F040 S2 documented assumption): Plain currently only ever authorizes a single workspace root, so this has not caused an observable issue, but a future multi-root search would need this addressed first.
Windows and Linux native packaging remains F120.
Zeroing the monaco-vscode-api bundle migration debt remains F110.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: File and content search honor ignore and include/exclude rules
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S2's Rust file search honors .gitignore with per-directory layering (deepest layer wins; negation and nested overrides both tested) and applies search.exclude/files.exclude via excludeGlobs, proven end-to-end by the S2 Browser E2E (a .gitignore-ignored sibling file never appears in Quick Open, its non-ignored sibling does and opens on Enter) and by S3 reusing the identical gitignore/exclude plumbing for text search. F040 S5 additionally: (a) registered a minimal, real search.exclude configuration schema default (`**/node_modules`, `**/bower_components`, `**/*.code-search`, matching upstream exactly) -- previously absent because Plain deliberately never imports the ~30-key search.contribution.js (F040 S1 decision, to avoid its Chat-context side effect), so every search had silently included node_modules unless a workspace's own .gitignore happened to cover it; (b) discovered and fixed that PlainSearchView's hand-built text-search query never applied any exclude pattern at all -- only Quick Open's file search did, via the pre-existing files.exclude default and upstream QueryBuilder plumbing. Text search now merges files.exclude/search.exclude the same way Quick Open does; both paths are proven together by the new Browser E2E ("excludes a node_modules directory from both Quick Open file search and Search view text search by default"). The `filePattern` include is a Rust-side case-insensitive subsequence prefilter, not upstream's includePattern glob syntax. Rust hardcodes "always honor .gitignore" and intentionally exposes no search.useIgnoreFiles/useGlobalIgnoreFiles/useParentIgnoreFiles schema, since neither side consumes such a flag (see platformGaps). Symlinks are never followed or reported as search results, proven by 3 Rust unit tests (S2) plus one browser-mock-level unit test; see platformGaps for why this specific behavior is not additionally exercised as a live Browser/Playwright scenario.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Results stream and cancel without blocking the UI
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S3 implemented the streaming text-search protocol (workspace_search_text_start/poll/cancel: an explicit wake signal plus front-end pull, with bounded queue backpressure) and proved it with Browser E2E covering grouped multi-file streaming render, click-to-editor navigation, a new query cancelling an in-flight one (asserted via exactly one cancel call and two start calls against the native IPC call log), a truncation banner past search.maxResults, and an invalid-regex Warning message -- none of it blocks the UI: typing, cancelling and re-querying all stay responsive even against the mock's artificial per-poll delay. File search (Quick Open, S2) is a bounded single request-response with a client-side 512-result cap and stale-response discarding while the user keeps typing. What Browser-mock evidence cannot prove is real elapsed-time search performance over a large real directory tree, or cancellation responsiveness against genuine Rust thread scheduling rather than a scripted mock delay; that real-disk-scale evidence is registered as E2E-004 in docs/e2e-handover.md (step 1) and has not yet been executed.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Replace plan validates file versions before writes
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S4's replace coordinator calls the exact same versioned wv1/PLR1/PLW1 save chain every manual edit already uses (ITextFileService.files.get(resource)?.save()), so a version conflict encountered during replace surfaces through the identical FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE path as any other save -- proven by the Browser E2E ("keeps a version-conflicted file's replace visibly failed while a sibling file's replace still succeeds"): the conflicted file's replace fails visibly (inline error, its match retained) while an unrelated sibling file's replace succeeds and is verified on disk. Per-match Replace, per-file Replace All in File, and global Replace All all route through the same coordinator; Replace and Replace All each have dedicated Browser E2E coverage (including one already-open editor kept in sync and one long-line absolute-column case), while Replace All in File shares that same code path without a dedicated scenario of its own (see platformGaps). Known, stated narrowing rather than a hidden gap: replace text is substituted literally with no $1-style capture-group backreferences; replacing across multiple files produces one independent undo entry per file rather than one shared cross-file undo group (a deliberate isolation trade-off so one file's failure never blocks or rolls back another); an over-8-MiB unopened file's replace fails visibly through the existing bulk-edit/working-copy read-limit path but has no dedicated Browser E2E of its own.

F050's own desktop matrix -- real system file-picker VSIX import, a real theme package fixture, cross-restart persistence of both the imported package library and the selected theme id, two hostile VSIX fixtures (zip-slip, no theme contributions) rejected with a desensitized toast and zero on-disk half-finished state, and removing the active imported theme falling back and clearing the persisted selection across a real restart -- is registered as E2E-005 in docs/e2e-handover.md and handed over to Codex for native execution; it has not yet been executed.
platformGaps: E2E-005 in docs/e2e-handover.md (real system file-picker VSIX import, cross-restart persistence of the imported library and the selected theme id, hostile VSIX rejection with on-disk verification, and remove-then-restart selection clearing) is handed over to Codex and not yet executed.

Imported theme packages never carry a contributes.themes[].id (S2's own manifest scope never captures a theme-level id at all): the registry and the persisted selection both use the resolved label (or a path-basename fallback) as the settingsId, matching upstream's own `settingsId = theme.id || label` fallback rule bit-for-bit rather than treating the missing field as a gap.

Icon themes and product icon themes (contributes.iconThemes/productIconThemes) are parsed and retained verbatim in the stored package record but never validated, resolved, or applied to any UI surface -- deliberately deferred whole to F060, now in_progress.

Plain does not follow the OS light/dark setting; the active theme only ever changes via explicit user selection (the Color Theme quick pick) or the one-time persisted-selection restore at boot -- a deliberate narrowing stated in the frozen research plan's exclusions, not an oversight.

There is no Settings UI of any kind; the persisted selection is exclusively read/written through the theme_get_selection/theme_set_selection command pair, never through a workbench.colorTheme configuration key (see docs/research/2026-07-24-theme-compatibility.md's decision 3 for why: the in-memory configuration service would still read a stale workbench.colorTheme value with no writer keeping it in sync, so no such key is ever registered).

installMultiRootNativeIpcMock (the separate multi-root Browser mock in tests/browser/workspace.spec.ts, independent of the installNativeIpcMock every theme scenario in this feature uses) still has no theme_list/theme_get_selection stubs -- a pre-existing S3 gap this slice did not need to close. Every multi-root scenario now additionally prints one theme_get_selection console.warn alongside S3's own theme_list one during bootstrap (both caught by the coordinator/picker's own best-effort fallback paths and asserted nowhere), rather than the assertions of any of those scenarios changing.

A persisted selection.plain.json file is a plain, non-package sibling directly under the theme library root, so once a selection has ever been written, Rust's own theme_list enumeration counts it toward its existing skipped tally (the same tolerance record::list_theme_packages already extends to a leftover staging directory) -- a benign accounting fact, covered by a dedicated Rust test, not a functional gap.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Import local VSIX and unpacked theme directory
acceptanceResults.result: F050 S1 built a bounded, capability-relative VSIX (zip) unpacker (zip crate, enclosed_name/is_symlink entry checks backstopped by Plain's own RelativePath::parse_wire since enclosed_name only catches `../` depth underflow and not absolute-path/drive-letter prefixes -- see the implementation-deviation record) with entry-count/per-entry/aggregate byte caps enforced against actually-read bytes, proven by 17 Rust tests covering zip-slip, symlink entries, oversized entries, oversized packages, zip bombs, corrupt/empty archives and clean round-trips; directory import (S1) shares the identical staging/limit machinery via an explicit non-recursive stack walk, covered by 4 more Rust tests. S2 layered manifest/theme-document validation on top (JSONC with exactly comments+trailing-commas, contributes.themes[] path/uiTheme validation, include-chain cycle/depth/file-count budgets, .tmTheme structural checks) with 19 further error-code tests. S3 exposed both paths as theme_import_vsix/theme_import_directory Tauri commands behind a real native file/directory picker, consumed end-to-end by the frontend (registerExtension/registerFileUrl against the imported package's own resource whitelist) and proven live by Browser E2E: importing a VSIX via the Command Palette shows a success toast and the new theme appears in the picker; a package already present from a prior session (via theme_list) reappears and applies for real at startup with its own distinctive editor.background. Real system file-picker exercise of both commands is registered as E2E-005, not yet executed.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Apply workbench colors and TextMate token colors
acceptanceResults.result: Plain never registers an extension-point handler at all (the upstream one is structurally unreachable under NullExtensionService, the root cause S0's own probe discovered and fixed): PlainThemeRegistry/PlainThemePicker construct ColorThemeData instances directly from each manifest's contributes.themes[] entry (built-in via getBuiltinExtensions(), imported via the S3 coordinator's local registerExtension/registerFileUrl call) and hand them straight to IWorkbenchThemeService.setColorTheme()'s own instanceof ColorThemeData fallback branch -- proven live by the S0 Browser E2E (`.monaco-workbench` carries real vs-dark/theme classes and a real `--vscode-editor-background` CSS variable instead of the previously-undiscovered unthemed placeholder) and by every subsequent slice's own scenarios reusing the identical apply path for imported themes. Applying colors requires a real IExtensionResourceLoaderService, which no existing override package provided (S0's own PlainExtensionResourceLoaderService closes that gap); token colors flow through the same ColorThemeData#ensureLoaded resource read. `.tmTheme` files are only structurally validated (S2), never parsed into token rules by this Rust domain -- token color application through .tmTheme (a tokenColors string reference) is exercised end-to-end by the S3 whitelist/registerFileUrl path but the actual TextMate scope-to-color resolution is entirely upstream Monaco/TextMate machinery this feature does not modify.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: JSONC, include and tmTheme fixtures pass
acceptanceResults.result: S2's manifest.rs parses package.json and every theme document with jsonc-parser configured for exactly `{allow_comments: true, allow_trailing_commas: true}` and every other option explicitly false (compile-time const-asserted, not just tested) -- deliberately narrower than upstream's looser JSON5-adjacent dialect. include chains are walked with an explicit visited-set (cycle rejection) and a depth cap of 32, plus a whole-package file-count budget of 64 shared across every contributes.themes[] entry's own chain -- both caps independent by design (see the frozen research doc's decision 2). `.tmTheme` files get a structural-only check (`<?xml` header + `<plist` + `<dict` presence) rather than a full plist parse, a deliberate scope line (the bytes are never executed or otherwise consumed by this Rust domain -- the real XML-to-token-rule parsing is Monaco/TextMate's own job downstream of the whitelist read). All of this is proven by 20 Rust theme_json tests plus 19 manifest tests covering the exact error-code closed set (23 codes through S3, 24 after S4's own THEME_SELECTION_INVALID addition) -- zip-slip, symlink entries, oversized/mis-shaped documents, include cycles/depth/file-count overruns, and out-of-manifest path references are all covered by dedicated, independently-constructed fixtures (no binary zip/plist files committed to the repo; every fixture is built in-process).

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Extension code is never executed

Confirmed by the full acceptance suite's own zero-Extension-Host architecture guard (scripts/plain/check-boundaries.mjs's fixed monaco-vscode-extensions-service-override import ban) staying green across every S0-S4 slice.

MAX_ICON_ASSOCIATIONS=4096 bounds the total icon/association count per document independently of the shared resources budget.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Unsafe SVG or missing icon IDs fall back safely
acceptanceResults.result: svg_sanitize.rs rejects <script>, on*= event attributes, <foreignObject>, external/javascript:/data: URLs and DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations in a single lower-cased scan (13 Rust tests), applied to every iconPath and any fonts[].src[] declaring format:"svg"; font_check.rs checks the remaining five formats against closed magic-byte signatures (8 Rust tests) and one Rust import.rs test proves a malicious SVG makes the whole package import fail atomically with zero residue, mirroring the identical zip-slip/oversized-package precedent. A file icon theme's own iconDefinitions structurally cannot reference an association Rust rejected (the association simply never enters the validated document), so 'missing icon ID' safety is a structural guarantee from S1's own validation rather than a runtime fallback branch; S3 additionally proved the two icon selection axes fall back safely and with zero crash when a persisted id matches nothing (own-axis warn, clear, and the already-applied vs-minimal/Default bootstrap default stands), independently of the color axis and of each other.

features.name: Rust PTY terminal
acceptance: Interactive shell supports input, resize, search and exit
Multiple tabs and splits clean up on window close
Backpressure and output fragmentation tests pass

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-25: cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings both zero-diff/zero-warning; cargo test 637/637 (up from 634 at the end of the multi-tab/split/scrollback slice -- +3 new: vt/tests.rs's escape-sequence-split-across-two-reads-at-every-one-of-17-boundaries test, its one-byte-at-a-time complement, and a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across two feed() calls, closing this slice's own fragmentation-evidence gap); pnpm exec vitest run 50 test files, 1024 cases (unchanged -- this slice touched no app/** source or test file); pnpm exec vite build 2150 bundle sources; node scripts/plain/check-boundaries.mjs 44 app sources / 89 Rust sources / 15 pinned runtime dependencies (all unchanged); node scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs 2150 sources, 203 tracked transitional debt sources (categories and debtSourceSha256 unchanged since the previous slice).

The 3 new Rust tests were additionally run standalone (cargo test terminal::vt::, 22/22 in that module) before being folded into the full suite above, and cargo fmt --check / cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings were re-run scoped to the terminal domain first and passed with zero diffs/warnings.

The one new Browser E2E scenario (a burst of 500 terminal output lines pushed with no yield in between, mirroring a real pty reader flooding output at OS speed) passed a focused repeat (--repeat-each=3, --retries=0, 3/3) before the full-suite run; the full pnpm exec playwright test --retries=0 suite then passed 63/63 (up from 62/62 at the end of the previous slice, the +1 being this new scenario), zero regressions.
nativeScenarios: F070's own real-desktop matrix -- a real interactive shell (input/output), resize against the WKWebView's actual layout pipeline, multiple tabs and a split each with an independently-alive real process, an untrusted workspace's real trust confirm/decline copy, and high-throughput commands (yes / cat over a large file) observed not to stall the UI or leave orphaned processes after window close -- is registered as E2E-007 in docs/e2e-handover.md and handed to Codex for native execution; it has not yet been executed.

Every other acceptance-relevant mechanism this feature needs -- the byte-level PTY<->VT flow-control gate's real pause/resume under load, the VT<->frontend single-frame emission credit, and VT-level parsing correctness across an escape sequence or a multi-byte UTF-8 character split at an arbitrary feed() boundary -- is proven directly against real subprocesses and the real libghostty-vt parser in src-tauri/src/terminal/{flow.rs,vt/tests.rs,service/tests.rs}, not only through Browser mock or native-desktop evidence. The Browser E2E suite additionally proves the frontend's own ack-driven backpressure path end to end (a 500-line burst mock, pushed with no yield in between) coalesces into a small, bounded number of real frame/ack round trips without dropping content or leaving the page unresponsive to further keyboard input -- but this remains a Chromium/mock-transport proof, not a WKWebView/real-process one, which is exactly what E2E-007 exists to close.
platformGaps: E2E-007 in docs/e2e-handover.md (the real desktop terminal matrix: real shell input/output, resize, multi-tab/split process lifecycle, untrusted-workspace trust copy, and high-throughput commands under real OS scheduling) is handed to Codex and not yet executed.

In-terminal find (half of the first acceptance's 'search') does not exist on either platform in the current implementation: plain-terminal-input.ts's own key encoder forwards Ctrl-modified keys (including Ctrl+F) as real terminal control sequences on Windows/Linux, and WKWebView provides no built-in in-page find the way a browser tab does on macOS -- discovered and recorded during the multi-tab/split/scrollback slice; only 'terminal text can be natively selected' is proven (Browser E2E), not 'terminal text can be found'.

Scrollback history rows carry no per-cell color -- the wire protocol's ScrollbackCell only ever carries bold/italic/underline-style booleans, never a resolved or palette-indexed color -- so history text always renders in the pane's current default foreground/background rather than its original color; a fix needs vt.rs to expose resolved colors off GridRef the way CellIteration already does for the live viewport, judged out of this feature's scope.

Splits are capped at 2 panes per tab and are not recursively subdividable; a pane viewing scrollback history does not automatically jump back to live on new output (only Shift+End or scrolling to the bottom does); both are deliberate, recorded MVP narrowings, not defects.

No shell integration (OSC 133/633) and no session persistence/reconnect across a restart; Windows/Linux native packaging remains F120 -- all stated up front in docs/research/2026-07-24-libghostty-terminal.md and unchanged by this closing slice.

libghostty-vt and its Rust binding are both pre-1.0 (breaking upstream API changes are possible) and the build depends on Zig 0.15.x plus a pinned, gitignored local Ghostty source checkout (.ghostty-vendor/) for offline reproducibility -- a real, disclosed supply-chain narrowing, not a hidden one.

Rendering stays DOM (the wterm-style MVP): the WebGL/beamterm upgrade path docs/research/2026-07-24-libghostty-terminal.md left open was evaluated against this slice's own real throughput evidence (see acceptanceResults[2]'s result) and judged unnecessary for now -- the single-frame emission credit already bounds the DOM renderer's paint rate to the display's own refresh rate regardless of how fast the pty itself produces bytes, and rows are painted as contiguous same-style <span> runs rather than one element per cell, bounding real DOM node count well below cols x rows. There is no real performance deficit driving an upgrade today; DOM MVP is judged sufficient and the upgrade is deferred rather than pursued speculatively.
Zeroing the monaco-vscode-api bundle migration debt remains F110.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Interactive shell supports input, resize, search and exit
acceptanceResults.result: Input: terminal_input_text (IME commit/paste) and terminal_input_key (structured key events encoded through libghostty-vt's own encoder) both write real bytes to the pty, proven against a real cat/cat -v subprocess (service/tests.rs's echo_round_trip_through_cat, input_key_writes_the_libghostty_encoded_bytes_to_the_pty) and the IME-specific Browser E2E 'sends only the final IME-committed text, never intermediate composition state'. Resize: terminal_resize propagates to the real pty (resize_takes_effect_and_is_observed_by_stty_size feeds a live stty size report back through the VT mirror) and to the frontend's own real layoutBody-driven measurement (Browser E2E 'resizes the terminal grid to match the panel's real size'). Exit: both a normal exit code and a killed/signaled exit are captured (a_normal_exit_code_is_captured, kill_immediate_tears_down_synchronously_and_captures_a_signal_exit) and reachable from the view via 'Plain: Kill Terminal' (Browser E2E). Search: a code-level re-audit during the multi-tab/split/scrollback slice found that neither platform's real product target supports in-terminal find under the current implementation (Ctrl+F is intercepted and forwarded as a real terminal control sequence on Windows/Linux; WKWebView has no built-in in-page find on macOS) -- only the other half of this acceptance's intent, that terminal text is discoverable/selectable, is proven (Browser E2E 'terminal output is real, selectable DOM text'); recorded as a known, deliberate gap (see platformGaps) rather than silently claimed as met.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Multiple tabs and splits clean up on window close
acceptanceResults.result: TerminalService has tracked sessions per window_label in a HashMap<String, HashMap<TerminalSessionId, Arc<TerminalSession>>> since the S1 slice, and close_window_kills_and_removes_every_session_for_that_window (service/tests.rs) proves close_window concurrently kills and joins every thread of every session for a window, synchronously, with no session left behind (a killed session's terminal_ack subsequently reports TERMINAL_SESSION_NOT_FOUND). The frontend's own multi-tab/split lifecycle (TerminalTabsModel, TerminalPaneController) is proven end to end by 4 Browser E2E scenarios: two tabs with independently-alive sessions where closing one leaves the other running, 'Plain: Kill Terminal' closing only the active tab, a split producing two independently-sized-and-sessioned panes, and a reload while multiple tabs (including a split) are open tearing down with zero pageerror. The real desktop process-tree confirmation of 'clean up on window close' -- shell-level ps verification that no orphaned child process survives a real Cmd+Q -- is registered as E2E-007 step 6 and not yet executed.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Backpressure and output fragmentation tests pass
acceptanceResults.result: Byte-level PTY->VT backpressure: flow.rs's own unit tests cover the high/low water mark hysteresis in isolation (stays_clear_below_the_high_water_mark, reaching_the_high_water_mark_pauses_until_the_low_water_mark, wait_until_clear_to_read_blocks_while_paused_and_unblocks_on_ack, cancel_wakes_a_paused_waiter_and_reports_cancelled, an_over_generous_ack_saturates_at_zero_rather_than_underflowing); service/tests.rs's output_well_beyond_the_high_water_mark_still_arrives_completely_and_in_order re-proves the same gate against a real subprocess generating ~112 KiB (2,200 lines) -- well beyond the 100,000-byte high water mark -- while continuously acking as a real frontend would, observes the reader was in fact paused, and asserts the final viewport content is byte-perfect with every frame's sequence number strictly consecutive (no gaps, no reordering, no silent drops). VT->frontend frame-level backpressure: FrameEmitGate's single-outstanding-frame credit is proven in pure unit tests (frame_emit_gate_single_credit_and_tolerant_ack_semantics, frame_emit_gate_does_not_spend_credit_or_a_sequence_number_on_a_clean_snapshot) and against a real session (frame_emission_is_gated_until_the_previous_frame_is_acked: a second frame does not appear until the first is acked, and the coalesced content fed in the meantime is exactly what the freed frame reports). Output fragmentation (this slice's own gap-fill): vt/tests.rs's feeding_an_escape_sequence_split_across_two_reads_parses_identically_regardless_of_the_split_point feeds the same SGR-plus-newline byte stream split into exactly two feed() calls at every one of its 17 possible byte offsets and asserts a byte-for-byte-identical DirtyFrame to a single whole feed() at every one; feeding_the_same_bytes_one_byte_at_a_time_produces_an_identical_dirty_frame_to_one_call repeats this at the worst-case one-byte-per-call granularity; feeding_a_multi_byte_utf8_character_split_across_two_feed_calls_still_decodes_correctly proves a 2-byte UTF-8 character (é) split exactly between its two bytes across two feed() calls still decodes to the complete character rather than mojibake or a dropped cell. A Browser E2E frontend-level complement ('a high-throughput burst of output is coalesced by the single-frame credit gate instead of stalling the UI or dropping content') pushes 500 lines with no yield in between through the same mocked single-credit gate the Rust FrameEmitGate mirrors, and proves the burst's last line still reaches the screen, the number of real terminal_ack round trips stays under 10 regardless of the 500 lines pushed (proving genuine coalescing, not just speed), and the page accepts further keyboard input immediately afterward. WebGL/beamterm upgrade judgment (the deferred decision point docs/research/2026-07-24-libghostty-terminal.md left open): not upgraded. The architecture's own single-frame emission credit already caps the DOM renderer's paint rate at whatever the display's refresh rate allows, independent of how fast the pty itself produces bytes -- a slow consumer only delays the next ack, which throttles frame production upstream rather than ever asking the DOM to paint faster than it can; the renderer additionally groups each row's cells into contiguous same-style <span> runs rather than one element per cell, bounding real DOM node count well below cols x rows. Combined with the real ~112 KiB/2,200-line throughput test and the 500-line Browser burst test above showing no stall and no dropped content under load, there is no real performance deficit driving a WebGL/beamterm upgrade today; DOM MVP is judged sufficient and the upgrade is deferred rather than pursued speculatively.
